hist-ea-01-c3.text: Sue Gronewald, Asia for Educators, Columbia University. The Ming Voyages. Asia for Educators, Columbia University.
hist-ea-01-c3.quote: But for the three last voyages, Zheng went even further, all the way to the east coast of Africa.
hist-ea-01-c3.claim: Zheng He's massive treasure fleets sailed as far as Africa, and then the voyages were halted.

hist-ea-01-c3.text: Columbia University, Asia for Educators. Taiping Rebellion (1850-1864). Asia for Educators, Columbia University.
hist-ea-01-c3.quote: It is estimated that the entire rebellion cost more than twenty million lives (twice that of World War I).
hist-ea-01-c3.claim: the Taiping Rebellion, which left ~20 million dead.

hist-ea-01-c2.text: Daniel C. Waugh (quoting Richard B. Mather, foreword to Xiong, Sui-Tang Chang'an, 2000). Chang'an (Xian). Silk Road Seattle, University of Washington.
hist-ea-01-c2.quote: At the height of its glory in the mid-eighth century, Chang'an was the most populous, cosmopolitan, and civilized city in the world
hist-ea-01-c2.claim: Walk into Chang'an during the Tang dynasty (618-907) and you'd be in the world's largest city.

hist-ea-01-c1.text: Michael Tsin (1995). Annotated Timeline of Chinese History. Asia for Educators, Columbia University.
hist-ea-01-c1.quote: Confucianism was established as orthodoxy and open civil service examinations were introduced.

hist-ea-01-c1.text: Joshua J. Mark (2020). Han Dynasty. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ea-01-c1.quote: the majority of ethnic Chinese refer to themselves as Han People (Han rem) proudly
hist-ea-01-c1.claim: Han influence went so deep that ethnic Chinese still call themselves 'Han'.

hist-ea-02-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2017). Heian Period. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ea-02-c1.quote: his rule would usher in the Kamakura Period (1185-1333 CE), also known as the Kamakura Shogunate, when Japanese government became dominated by the military.
hist-ea-02-c1.claim: The Kamakura period (1185-1333) saw the rise of samurai warrior class and shogun military government.

hist-ea-02-c2.text: Graham Squires (2022). Meiji Restoration. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ea-02-c2.quote: In 1853, the American commander Mathew Perry (1794-1858) sailed a fleet of 'black ships' to Japan and demanded that the country open up ports for trade.
hist-ea-02-c2.claim: Commodore Perry's American gunboats in 1853 forced Japan open.

hist-ea-02-c2.text: Graham Squires (2022). Meiji Period. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ea-02-c2.quote: Following the overthrow of the Tokugawa shogunate in the Meiji Restoration of 1868, Japan's new leaders embarked on a program of radical reform aimed at strengthening the country so it could resist the threat of European imperialism.
hist-ea-02-c2.claim: Recognizing the threat, Japan rapidly modernized in the Meiji Restoration (1868).

hist-ea-04-c2.text: history.state.gov. Milestones in the History of U.S. Foreign Relations - Office of the Historian. history.state.gov.
hist-ea-04-c2.quote: On October 1, 1949, Chinese Communist leader Mao Zedong declared the creation of the People’s Republic of China (PRC).
hist-ea-04-c2.claim: The People's Republic was proclaimed in 1949.
